title: Betting on Leading Tech Giants Pays Off Big: Dubai Billionaire Reveals Investments in OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic Raked in Billions of Dollars
excerpt: In recent years, early investors who have actively bet on global frontier technology giants are reaping generous returns. According to Bloomberg, Hussain Sajwan
content_html:
In recent years, early investors who have actively bet on global frontier technology giants are reaping generous returns. According to Bloomberg, Hussain Sajwani, a well-known Dubai billionaire and founder of Damac Group, recently said publicly at the Bloomberg Dubai Investment Forum that by investing in just three highly watched tech companies—OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic—they have already reaped billions of dollars in huge gains.

From Traditional Real Estate to the Tech Frontier: Diversified Investments Show Results

Damac Group started out in Dubai's real estate business and accumulated vast wealth alongside years of prosperity in Dubai's property market. According to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, Sajwani's current personal net worth exceeds $13 billion. However, while consolidating its traditional strengths, Damac Group has clearly accelerated its strategic pace in recent years, gradually expanding its investment blueprint into high-tech and digital infrastructure.

In today's capital markets, these frontier tech companies have demonstrated exceptionally strong ability to attract capital and growth expectations. Take Anthropic, which is about to make a push into the capital markets: its IPO process is currently several times oversubscribed, and the market has shown sustained enthusiasm for what could become one of the largest tech IPOs in history.

Sober Reflection Behind the Boom: High Valuations Fuel Market Worries and Divergence

Although Sajwani and other early investors have made a fortune from this wave of technology, as valuations have risen, market concerns about whether AI company valuations are too high have also been heating up. Sajwani candidly acknowledged that while the AI industry will continue to generate substantial revenue in the future, the possibility of a market correction cannot be entirely ruled out.

At the same time, affected by geopolitical factors (such as the war in Iran), demand in Dubai's local real estate market has slowed to some extent in recent months, which has also led investors to focus more on long-term infrastructure arrangements.

During discussions at the same forum, industry experts offered different perspectives on future investment directions:

Blackstone's Bullish Outlook: Farhad Karim, Global COO of Blackstone's Private Wealth business, pointed out that digital infrastructure and logistics offer particularly prominent investment opportunities. In the future, computing power demand driven by the AI boom will grow substantially, and the region's continued investment in related areas is very encouraging.

PIMCO's Cautious Expectations: By contrast, Christian Stracke, Managing Director and President of Pacific Investment Management Company (PIMCO), appeared more cautious. He expects growth in global digital infrastructure lending to gradually slow, and noted that even if capital continues to flow into the market, investment demand is unlikely to experience explosive year-after-year doubling.
